title: From Reading Code to Reading Spec: A Verified Layer for LLM-Driven Codebase Maintenance
abstract: arXiv:2609.06383v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The rapid growth of LLM-generated code increases software complexity and the maintenance burden on engineers. While LLMs offer a potential automated alternative, this structural complexity hinders their ability to manage codebases directly. We introduce the Provable Representation Of Original Functionality (PROOF), which manages codebases indirectly via structured specifications. To enable full-lifecycle codebase management strictly through these specifications, PROOF abstracts codebase topology into a hierarchical natural-language representation. To establish absolute trust, the system proves semantic equivalence by reconstructing source code exclusively from this specification. This verified foundation drives maintenance requests, executing code modifications while synchronously updating itself to prevent semantic drift. Experiments on real-world repositories confirm the effectiveness of these specifications.

translated_title: 从读代码到读规约：面向LLM驱动的代码库维护的验证层
translated_abstract: LLM生成代码的快速增长加剧了软件的复杂性，并加重了工程师的维护负担。虽然LLM提供了一种潜在的自动化替代方案，但这种结构性复杂性阻碍了它们直接管理代码库的能力。我们提出了原始功能可证明表示（PROOF），它通过结构化规约间接地管理代码库。为了严格地通过这些规约实现代码库的全生命周期管理，PROOF将代码库拓扑抽象为分层的自然语言表示。为了建立绝对的信任，该系统通过仅从规约重构源代码来证明语义等价性。这一经过验证的基础驱动维护请求，在执行代码修改的同时同步更新自身，以防止语义漂移。在真实世界代码库上的实验证实了这些规约的有效性。
tldr: 论文提出PROOF系统，将代码库拓扑抽象为分层自然语言规约，并通过从规约重构源代码来证明语义等价，使LLM能够借助规约间接、可靠地执行代码库维护并防止语义漂移。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces PROOF, which abstracts codebase topology into hierarchical natural-language specifications and proves semantic equivalence by reconstructing source code from them, enabling LLMs to reliably maintain codebases without semantic drift.
